title: ANNEXURE C: FREEDOM FIGHTERS OF ODISHA

blocks.content: The resistance movements in Odisha, from the Paika Rebellion of 1817 to the Quit India Movement of 1942, demonstrated unparalleled courage and sacrifice in India's freedom struggle.

rows: Commander of the King of Khordha; led armed uprising against British forces
Tribal and regional leader who resisted annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse
Titled 'Utkal Mani'; founder of Satyabadi Bana Vidyalaya and Samaja newspaper
Tribal leader executed by the British in Berhampur Jail in 1943
Youngest martyr (age 12) of the Indian freedom struggle

items: The Paika Rebellion (1817) led by Baxi Jagabandhu is frequently tested in competitive exams as an early precursor to the 1857 revolt.
Utkal Sammilani, established by Madhusudan Das ('Utkal Gaurav') in 1903, was instrumental in making Odisha the first state formed on a linguistic basis in 1936.
Laxman Nayak is often referred to in exam questions as the 'Gandhi of Malkangiri' for leading non-violent tribal agitation.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Baxi Jagabandhu led the Paika Rebellion of 1817, an early armed uprising against British land revenue policies in Khordha.
Veer Surendra Sai organized a prolonged resistance against British forces in Sambalpur, opposing annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse.
Pandit Gopabandhu Das, known as 'Utkal Mani', founded Satyabadi Bana Vidyalaya and spearheaded the Non-Cooperation Movement in Odisha.
Laxman Nayak mobilised the tribal population of Koraput during the Quit India Movement of 1942 before his execution in 1943.
Baji Rout, a 12-year-old boatboy from Dhenkanal, became India's youngest martyr after refusing to ferry British soldiers across the Brahmani River.
